post.summary: List the nodes of one package or runtime symbol.
post.description: Lists the syntax nodes of one package or runtime symbol with their source text, in the exact release its identity names: each declaration's item node, then the descendants that belong to that declaration and not to a declaration nested in it, outermost first per declaration. Every node's `unit` is a source unit of that release. The request carries `symbol` and MAY carry `node_cursor` and `view`; the server refuses `path`, `position`, and `rev`. A page holds at most `page_limit_max` nodes and, beyond its first node, at most `x-rift-page-source-bytes-max` bytes of node source; `node_cursor` continues where the page stopped. A symbol the release does not declare answers 404.

post.description: Returns the matches of one regular expression over the source files of selected exact package versions, in package order as the request lists them, then file path order, then match offset. The server verifies candidate files in that order and stops a page at `limit` hits, at `x-rift-page-files-max` files, or at `x-rift-page-text-bytes-max` bytes of verified text, whichever comes first; `next_cursor` continues where the page stopped, and a `result_truncated` warning names the bound.

post.description: Finds declarations holding source positions in one immutable selection. Answers each position once, retaining request order and one shared captured view. A position in a type stub may name a declaration with a proved runtime or package owner. Complete captured coverage with no declaration returns missing; unavailable coverage returns unavailable. The server MUST NOT answer from another version, and MUST NOT move a position past its line or the text, or one inside a character, to a neighboring one.

registry.description:
Canonical registry endpoint, including its path when that path identifies the registry.
Credentials, query and fragment are never part of this owner.

PackageIdentity.description: One package as its package manager identifies it.

SourceUnitId.description: Physical source identity with a defining package or runtime owner, or a source resolver and canonical unit key. It names no revision: a read selects the revision whose bytes it answers. The codec validates decoded paths, UTF-8 and canonical percent-encoding before lookup.

SymbolId.description: Canonical logical symbol identity with local, profile, registered local, registered local profile, package or runtime ownership. A package or runtime owner names no version: a release revision selects one. The portable codec validates owner coordinates, UTF-8 and canonical percent-encoding before lookup.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this Symbol across the whole workspace. Absent for an
unestablished symbol: no accepted evidence, or more than one, established its
identity.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

name.description:
The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered
signatures live in `signatures`.

kind.description:
What this symbol is in the provider's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or
`table`.

facets.description:
Portable classification for cross-language queries, absent when empty. The local
kinds `trait` and `interface` can both carry the `type` facet.

origin.description:
Where the declaration belongs and how it was produced. Absent when it says a
project declaration, authored, with no package - the common case.

container.description:
The symbol this one belongs to - the class that owns a method, the module that owns
a function. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method sits beside its type and a Rust
method inside an `impl` block, both naming the type here; absent at the top level.

modifiers.description:
Language keywords qualifying the declaration: `export`, `async`, `const`. Absent
when empty.

visibility.description:
How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms - `public`, `private`,
`pub(crate)`. Absent where the language has no such concept.

types.description:
The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a
field type, a bound. Absent when empty.

signatures.description:
One entry per callable form, absent when empty. Where the language dispatches
overloads separately they are separate symbols joined by the `overloads` edge;
several entries here are alternative forms of one dispatch target, as
`typing.overload` writes them.

documentation.description:
Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written
in. Absent when empty.

extensions.description:
Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the provider that
emitted them. Absent when empty.

document_local.description:
Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The
provider classifies locality from its language model; absent when `false`.

Symbol.description:
Readable Symbol assembled from normalized Contributions. Source structure lives in Node
and is connected through Relationship.

location.description:
Which of the four places the declaration belongs. Absent exactly when
`source_kind` is `synthetic`.

package.description:
The package that owns the declaration: present for `dependency`, and optionally
for `project`. Absent for `stdlib`, `external`, and a synthetic declaration.

runtime.description:
Exact runtime or compiler release that owns a standard-library declaration.
Mutually exclusive with `package`.

source_kind.description: Whether the declaration is authored, generated, or synthetic.

SymbolOrigin.description:
Where a symbol belongs and how its declaration came to exist. Source location and
generation are separate: generated code can belong to the project or to a dependency.
Absent from `Symbol` entirely when it says a project declaration, authored, with no
package.

SourceKind.description: How source or a declaration came to exist.
x-enum-descriptions: A person wrote it.
A tool produced it from other source.
The provider minted it without any source text.

SourceLocationKind.description:
Which of the four places a declaration's source belongs, on `SymbolOrigin`. Package
ownership is the separate `package` field: a `project` declaration can carry one too,
and `dependency` always does.
x-enum-descriptions: Owned by the current workspace.

Owned by one resolved dependency. The ECMAScript built-ins, such as `Array`, belong
to the npm `typescript` package, whose `lib.*.d.ts` files declare them.

Installed with the language toolchain: `stdlib/rust`, `stdlib/node`, or
`stdlib/python`.
Outside the project, dependency graph, and standard library.

Language.description: A language name and its optional dialect, joined by `:`. `sql` and `sql:postgresql` are two languages with two symbol spaces.

text.description: The body of the comment, with the comment syntax stripped.

Documentation.description: One block of documentation attached to a declaration, in the markup it was written in.

DocumentationFormat.description:
Which markup the text is written in, since whoever displays a doc comment is the one that
renders it.
x-enum-descriptions: Plain text with no markup to render.
Markdown as authored in the source.

Extensions.description:
Facts a provider carries that the model has no field for, under a reverse-domain key.
Keys and values use RFC 8785 canonical JSON. Consumers skip entries they do not
implement.

version.description:
Which version of the key's advertised schema shaped `data`. A consumer skips a value
whose version it does not implement.

data.description:
The value itself, shaped by whatever that key and version advertise. Rift carries it
and never interprets it.

ExtensionValue.description:
Versioned extension value. data is validated against the schema advertised for its key
and version.

SymbolFacet.description:
One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are
shared, so a filter written once applies to every served language.

ExactKind.description: A provider-local kind preserving the construct name used by that language implementation.

display.description: The signature as a reader sees it, in the language's own syntax.

links.description:
Symbols named inside `display`, each with the byte range of `display` that names it,
so a renderer can turn the rendered text into links. Absent when empty.

language.description: The language whose syntax `display` is written in.

receiver.description:
The implicit first parameter - `self`, `this`. Absent for a free function, and for
languages that have no such thing.

parameters.description: Declared parameters, in source order. Absent when empty.

returns.description:
What the call yields, absent when empty. An array because a language may return
several values, and because a declared and an inferred return are separate
bindings.

type_parameters.description:
The generic parameters this form declares, each as the symbol that declares it.
Absent when empty.

throws.description: Types this form declares it can raise. Absent when empty.

effects.description:
Effect keywords the declaration carries, in the language's own words: `async`,
`unsafe`, `pure`. The spelling is preserved and never mapped onto a portable
meaning; absent when empty.

extensions.description:
Signature facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted
them. Absent when empty.

Signature.description:
One callable form of a symbol: the text it renders as, the symbols that text points at,
and its structure. Overloads are separate entries.

name.description:
What the parameter is called. Absent where the language allows an unnamed one, as
a positional parameter in a function type.

types.description:
What it accepts, absent when empty. An array because a declared type and an
inferred one are separate bindings.

optional.description: Whether a call may leave it out.

variadic.description: Whether it absorbs the arguments that follow - `*args`, `...rest`.

default.description: The default value as written in the source. Absent where there is none.

extensions.description:
Parameter facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted
them. Absent when empty.

Parameter.description:
One parameter of a `Signature`: what it is called, the types bound to it, and how a call
may pass it. A receiver is one of these too, held in its own field because it has no
position in the parameter list.

role.description: The role this type plays for the symbol.

origin.description: Where the type fact came from.

TypeBinding.description: One type a symbol carries, together with the role it plays for that symbol.

TypeBindingRole.description: What this type is to the symbol that carries it.

TypeBindingOrigin.description:
Where the type fact came from. A declared type and an inferred one can both be present
and disagree, which is the interesting case.
x-enum-descriptions: Written in the source by the author.
Worked out by the provider from usage.
Required by the surrounding context.

language.description: The language the spelling is in, and so which provider produced it.

source.description: The type as it is written: `Optional[Config]`, `&mut [u8]`, `string | null`.

resolved.description:
The symbol that declares this type, where one does. Absent for a structural type,
which has a spelling and nothing to open.

extensions.description:
Type facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted them.
Absent when empty.

TypeExpression.description:
How a type is written in the source, plus the symbol that declares it when one does. A
type with a declaration resolves to that symbol; a structural type - `string | null`,
`{ a: string }` - has the spelling and nothing to resolve to.

range.description: Offsets into the rendered string in `Signature.display`.

symbol.description: The symbol that stretch of text names.

SignatureLink.description:
One symbol named inside a rendered signature, with the byte range of that rendering which
names it.

start.description: First byte of the range, counted from the start of the file.

end.description:
One past the last byte. Equal to `start` for an empty range, which is how a position
between two bytes is spelled.

TextRange.description:
Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets over authoritative UTF-8 source. Every provider converts
from whatever its toolchain counts in at its own boundary, so two toolchains' column
numbers arrive here on the same scale. No JSON Schema keyword can tie one field to
another, so that `end` is never below `start` is asserted by the surface
validation tests instead.

registry.description: Accepted registry endpoint. Absent for a path, Git repository or direct URL source.

version.description: The exact version a lockfile pins. Absent when only a manifest names the package.

requirement.description:
The version requirement a manifest declares. Absent when a lockfile pins the

PackageContextEntry.description:
One package the workspace depends on, as its manifests and lockfiles state it.

Entries order by manager, then name, then the selector they state: a declared

PackageAvailability.description:
Whether a global package index can answer for one package, and where the entry's

The entry names a package a public registry serves, crates.io, npm, or the

The entry names a path outside the workspace, or an archive at a path, that only

The entry names a git repository.
The entry names a registry other than the public one its package manager reads.

The entry names a package fetched from a URL no registry serves, such as a uv

target.description: Which package results may be returned. Omitted, symbol.

view.description: A view returned by a preceding read. Expiry never selects latest implicitly.

contributing_fields.description: Fields that contributed to ranking. `file_content` names a match inside the declaration, which the file's text holds.

The server **MUST** retain the captured view and its original expiry on every page, including an empty page.

packages.description: Selected exact package versions. Omitted or empty, use the newest collected stable version of each package, or its newest prerelease when no stable version is collected.

oneOf.description: A valid identifier stored in the notebook.

index.description: Position among every cell, including unselected cells.

oneOf.description: The cell's zero-based position in its notebook.

NotebookCellIdentity.description: The authored cell identifier or its position when no identifier exists.

NotebookCellKind.description: The selected notebook cell's content kind.
x-enum-descriptions: Markdown source decoded from a markdown cell.
Source decoded from a code cell, without execution.

ProjectPath.description:
One path below the workspace root, using forward slashes and UTF-8 in Unicode NFC - Rift
normalizes what it emits and what it accepts, and compares byte-for-byte. The empty path
names the root itself. Absolute paths, backslashes, control characters, empty segments,
and `.` or `..` segments are refused before the filesystem is touched. The limit is 1000
UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A workspace holding two entries whose NFC forms are equal
fails the read that touches them with `content_unavailable`.

PackageDocumentationHit.description: One documentation block returned by search.

source.description: The block source excerpt when requested, bounded across the response page.

view.description:
The immutable view that supplied this hit. The caller passes its `id` to later
exact, source, declaration, and relationship reads to retain the same context.
Absent when the caller selected latest facts without retained serving context.

hit.description:
What was found. A symbol, a file, a documentation block, or a commit -
whichever `target` allowed.

score.description:
The ranking value attached to this hit and used to merge duplicate hits.
Exact original identifier spelling ranks before this value under `relevance`.
Present on the wire when `include` names `score`; comparable within one answer
and nowhere else.

matched_by.description: Which indexed fields produced the match. Absent when empty.

source.description:
The source text around the hit, requested with `include: ["source"]`. Covers the
hit's `range`; a caller that needs the range already has it there.

range.description:
Byte range of the hit within `path` or `unit`. Absent for a symbol whose source is
unavailable or synthetic.

line.description: The 1-based source line where the hit begins, or absent with `range`.

path.description:
Project-relative path of the hit, present for a project file hit and for a symbol
hit whose declaration belongs to the project. A hit in a dependency or
standard-library file carries `unit` in its place.

unit.description:
Source-catalog unit of a hit in a dependency or standard-library file: a
declaration, or a `pattern` match. A hit in a file carries exactly one of `path` and
`unit`; a commit hit carries neither.

traversal_path.description:
Shortest relationship path to this hit, present when a traversal reached it,
including a hit also matched lexically.

distance.description:
Number of edges in `traversal_path`. It is present exactly when `traversal_path` is
present and equals its length.

change.description:
How the declaration differs between the two sides `change` named, present when the
comparison produced this hit. The hit's `hit.symbol`, `path`, `range`, `line`, and
`source` read the head side, except for a removed declaration, which keeps its
base-side identity, path, range, and source - the head side no longer holds it. A
change hit carries no `score`, since a comparison ranks nothing.

SearchHit.description:
One search hit. Its file, symbol, documentation, or commit payload carries the canonical
identity. Dependency and synthetic symbols can have no readable source; file hits cannot.

seed.description: The declaration the walk starts at. The seed itself is never a hit.

direction.description:
Which edges the walk follows from each visited symbol: `incoming` reaches the
declarations referencing it, `outgoing` the declarations it calls. Omitted, `incoming`.

facets.description:
Portable relationship facets eligible for the walk. Omitted or empty, every facet is
eligible.

depth.description: Hops the walk may take from `seed`. The server accepts 1 or 2. Omitted, 1.

to.description:
When set, the answer keeps only the hit whose walk reaches this symbol. That hit's
path is the shortest one the walk found. A `to` the walk cannot reach within `depth`
answers empty, not refused.

SearchTraversal.description:
A bounded relationship walk starting at one symbol.

From `seed`, the server visits its neighbors, then their neighbors, up to `depth` hops,
following `direction` and narrowed to `facets`; each reached symbol keeps the shortest
path the walk found to it.

kind.description: What the head revision did to the declaration.

base_path.description:
Where the declaration lived at the base revision. Absent for a declaration the head
revision introduced.

head_path.description:
Where the declaration lives at the head revision. Absent for a declaration the head
revision removed.

SymbolChange.description:
How one declaration differs between the two compared revisions, and where it lives on
each side.

documentation.description: Block, source, and collector revision answering this match.

oneOf.description: A documentation block projected from an existing text or symbol document.
A symbol hit: the declaration a provider resolved.

languages.description:
Distinct `Language` values that read this file, sorted by name and dialect.
Absent when empty.

oneOf.description: A file hit: one entry of the tree, whether or not any provider reads it.
A commit hit: one commit the history store holds, matched by its message.

SearchHitTarget.description: What a search hit is. Tagged, so the payload correlation survives code generation.

MatchedField.description: Which indexed field produced a search hit.
x-enum-descriptions: A declaration's name, qualified name, or a term derived from them matched.
A rendered signature matched.
An attached doc comment matched.
The file's contents matched.

The vector ranking placed the hit, and no indexed field carries the query's
literal bytes. A hit any other ranking placed names the field that carried it
instead.
The project-relative path matched.
A relationship traversal reached the hit.
A comparison `change` named found the declaration changed.

relationship.description: The relationship followed for this step.

direction.description: How the walk followed the directed relationship.

GraphHop.description:
One auditable step in a search traversal. `relationship` retains its occurrence and
derivation; `direction` records how the walk followed it.

TraversalDirection.description:
Which edge direction a search traversal walks from each visited symbol. A language
engine supplies the edges of both: its references for `incoming`, its call hierarchy for
`outgoing`.
x-enum-descriptions:
Walks edges arriving at each visited symbol: the references a language engine
resolves to it, each hop carrying the `references` facet.

Walks edges leaving each visited symbol: the calls a language engine's call
hierarchy names for it, each hop carrying the `calls` facet.

revision.description: The commit id, as the workspace's version control spells it.

message.description: The commit message, cut at `COMMIT_MESSAGE_BYTES_MAX` bytes on a character boundary.

message_truncated.description:
Whether the message ran past `COMMIT_MESSAGE_BYTES_MAX` bytes, so `message` holds
its first bytes alone.

author.description: Who authored the commit, as the version control records it.

timestamp.description:
When the commit was committed, as RFC 3339 date-time carrying the recorded offset:
the committer time, not the author time.

paths.description:
The paths the commit changed against the commit it was compared with, in path order,
at most `COMMIT_PATHS_MAX`. A path `[source]` leaves out of the index, or a lockfile
`[search.text] excluded_lockfiles` names, is not listed.

paths_truncated.description: Whether the commit changed more paths than `paths` lists.

CommitHit.description: One commit whose message matched a commit search, as the history store holds it.

HopDirection.description: How one path step followed its directed relationship.
x-enum-descriptions: The walk followed the edge from source to target.
The walk followed the edge against its direction, from target to source.

from.description: The symbol the edge starts at.

kind.description:
What the edge is in this provider's vocabulary, such as `import`, `use`, or
`implements`.

facets.description:
Portable classification, so a query for `imports` finds local kinds such as `import`
and `use` alike.

to.description:
The symbol the edge points at. One Rift cannot read carries the `external` origin;
the edge is the same either way.

occurrence.description:
Exact physical occurrence when this edge was read from source, independent of
whether the provider supplied a source node.

confidence.description:
How likely a `heuristic` edge is to hold, from 0 to 1. Absent for any other
derivation.

producer.description:
The external producer that emitted the edge, named by a package publication that
carries its facts. Absent for an edge Rift's own analysis produced.

extensions.description:
Edge facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted them.
Absent when empty.

Relationship.description:
One directed edge between two symbols. Its occurrence is where it was read from, and its
derivation is how much the provider knew when it was read.

RelationshipDerivation.description:
How this edge was established. Every edge reaches Rift from a provider, and this field
records whether the provider resolved the edge semantically, read it from syntax, or
inferred it.
x-enum-descriptions: The provider resolved the edge semantically, so a consumer may act on it directly.
The edge was read from syntax alone, without semantic resolution.
The edge is a guess, qualified by `confidence`.

DocumentationDigest.description: Full lowercase SHA-256 digest for documentation content and identity.

RuntimeIdentity.description: One exact runtime or compiler release.

id.description: Selects the same workspace, owner, applicability and accepted index revision.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry. The service retains the view's required facts until this time.

CapturedView.description: The immutable serving view and the expiry promised by its owner.

CapturedViewId.description: A service-issued key for one immutable view in one serving context.

CommitAuthor.description:
The author one revision records, as committed: no `.mailmap` rewrites the name or the
address.

id.description: Canonical logical object, including proved runtime or stub mappings.

kind.description: Declaration kind in the provider's vocabulary.

revision.description:
The release of the declaration's owner that `id` answers in. It differs from
the position's release when a proved stub mapping names a runtime declaration.

oneOf.description: An established declaration holds this exact position.
Complete captured coverage contains no declaration at this position.

view.description: Selected view, when one could be captured.

oneOf.description: Presence or absence cannot be established at this exact position.

DeclarationPositionResult.description: One submitted source position and its exact declaration outcome.

Duration.description: A duration: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`.

position_encoding.description: Character units negotiated by the engine that supplied the positions.

positions.description: Positions to answer once, retaining request order.

view.description: A preceding immutable selection shared by the whole batch.

FindDeclarationsParams.description: Finds declarations holding positions in one immutable selection.

warnings.description: Typed read warnings, including explicit partial coverage.

FindDeclarationsResult.description: One answer per submitted position, retaining one shared captured selection.

GetSymbolInclude.description: One optional `get_symbol` hit field the caller may opt into through `include`.
x-enum-descriptions: The hit's version-control timeline.
Bounded documentation referring to the exact declaration.

id.description: Canonical identity. Ownership and language come from this address.

include.description:
Requested projections. Omitted or empty requests none. A declaration's source is read
by `nodes` with `symbol`.

revision.description:
The revision to read. A git revision reads that commit of a project, a tree
revision reads the served working tree, and a release revision selects the release
of a package or runtime `id`'s owner. Omitted reads the served working tree, or for
a package the version the workspace's dependencies pin, else the newest collected
release. The server refuses it beside `view` and once the index no longer serves it.

view.description: A view returned by a preceding read. Expiry never selects latest implicitly.

declaration_limit.description: Most declarations returned in this read. Omitted uses the existing five-item bound.

declaration_cursor.description: Continuation bound to this exact symbol, projections and serving view.

GetSymbolParams.description: Reads one exact logical symbol obtained from discovery or another read.

symbol.description: One logical symbol. Its established `id` is required by read validation.

view.description: The immutable context used for this result and its continuations.

revision.description: The revision this answer was read at: a commit, a release, or a working tree.

declarations.description: Declaration bindings in deterministic source order.

declaration_cursor.description: Continuation for remaining declarations in this exact view.

history.description: Requested timeline for the logical symbol.

warnings.description: Projection cuts and other typed read warnings.

oneOf.description: The exact identity was established, even when it has no source declarations.

symbol_not_found.description: Definite exact miss and its actual structural candidates.

revision.description: The revision this answer was read at: a commit, a release, or a working tree.

oneOf.description: The valid identity is absent from the completely searched exact selection.

view.description: The selected view, when one could be captured.

revision.description: The revision the read selected, when it established one.

oneOf.description: The exact selection cannot establish presence or absence.

GetSymbolResult.description: Exactly one logical object, definite absence, or explicit selection unavailability.

GlobalPageWarningCode.description: Stable conditions a global package page can report while returning valid items.
x-enum-descriptions: The service narrowed a query before ranking.
The service omitted source content at its source bound.
The publication changed while pages were assembled.
A requested capability was unavailable.

The service returned a code this client does not know.

PositionEncoding.description: How a language engine counts characters within a source line.
x-enum-descriptions: UTF-8 bytes.
UTF-16 code units.

unit.description: Physical source unit, paired with `range`, or absent for a source-less object.

qualified_name.description: Full original qualified name of the retained object.

field.description: Public field whose bound the object crossed.

oneOf.description:
One object crossed a public field bound. Its original facts remain retained;
every other admitted object can answer.

unit.description: The source whose framework context is unresolved.

framework.description: The framework whose context could not be established.

detail.description: The missing package version, configuration, or template source.

oneOf.description:
Framework context could not be resolved for one source. Ordinary syntax stands;
framework-specific facts whose context is missing are left out.

name.description: The declaration name the caller requested.

alternatives.description: Project declaration identities the caller can use to select another name.

detail.description:
Why closest declarations could not be selected within the work bound.
Absent when every selected declaration was compared or scope is `global`.

oneOf.description:
The lookup found no declaration under its name, language, and scope.
`alternatives` names up to three project declarations, ordered by the smallest
case-insensitive Unicode Levenshtein distance to their short or qualified names.
Equal distances use qualified name, then project path order. Revision reads
use that revision's declarations. A `global` lookup carries no alternatives;
an `all` lookup proposes project declarations alone. If complete closest ranking
exceeds `search.symbol_alternatives_work`, alternatives are empty and `detail`
carries the registered failure's message, recovery action, and observed work.

warning.description: Bounded source identity, stage, failure label, and omitted count.

oneOf.description: Documentation collection or excerpt output omitted part of a selected source.

detail.description:
Which documentation was left out and the bound it crossed - prose for a
reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The documentation this read projects onto crossed a bound, so no documentation
block joins the answer: declarations and files answer as they would without it.
The condition holds until the documentation it names changes.

index_tree_revision.description: Tree revision the published index covers.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The answer was computed from an index that lags the tree the read captured. Facts
derived from the index may miss the newest writes; the digests state which two
trees disagree. When the two digests are equal, the tree moved in recorded files
outside the syntax-indexed ones or in the configuration file, and `detail` says
which.

prepared.description: Declarations of the captured tree that already carry a vector.

total.description: Declarations the set being embedded holds.

ready_in.description:
Estimated wait before the vector ranking joins an answer, not a measurement
of this machine. A caller may report it and must not schedule against it.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The vector ranking holds no vectors for the tree this read captured, so the answer
was ranked lexically alone. The pass over that tree is still running, or the tree
was published after the corpus the ranking holds was described. `prepared` and
`total` state how far the ranking has got for the captured tree, and `ready_in` is
derived from workspace size and embedding progress.

prepared.description: Selected workspace files whose capture and analysis have finished.

total.description: Selected workspace files, once discovery has finished.

ready_in.description: Estimated wait before local preparation finishes. No estimate is available yet.

detail.description: Why the local index is preparing - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The local index is still preparing selected workspace files. The answer covers only
files whose capture and analysis have finished; `total` is absent until discovery ends.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The vector ranking will not answer for the life of this server, so every answer
is ranked lexically alone. No retry is coming: fix the `[search.vector]`
configuration and start the server again.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The full-text tier did not rank this answer, so it came from identifier matching
alone: a query phrased as prose finds nothing. The tier is still committing the
captured tree, missed a commit, holds no indexed tree, failed to load, got no
database connection within `[search] busy_timeout`, or still answers for a newer
publication after the request's capture attempts; `detail` names which, and what
clears it.

terms_max.description:
Terms and quoted phrases the query was cut to: the server's bound on one
parsed query.

oneOf.description:
The query carried more terms and quoted phrases than `terms_max`, so the server
dropped the shortest unquoted terms and ranked the answer by the rest. Every
quoted phrase is kept. Shorten `query`, or quote the terms that must be matched.

matches_max.description: Units the ranking stopped at: the server's bound on one lexical ranking.

oneOf.description:
The lexical ranking stopped at `matches_max` units; hits past it never reached the
page, whatever `paths` selects. Narrow `query`.

results_max.description:
The bound the read stopped at: the server's limit on both the candidates one
read ranks and the hits it returns.

oneOf.description:
The server reached `results_max`, its result bound, before ordering and paging:
what the bound cut never reaches any page, and `total_pages` counts only what fit.
The bound cuts the ranked candidates and the hit set alike. The warning means the
bound was reached; a set of exactly `results_max` hits carries it too. Narrow
`query` or `paths`.

matches_per_file.description: Matches one file contributes at most: the server's bound on one file's matches.

files.description: The files cut at the bound.

oneOf.description:
A file held more matches of `pattern` than `matches_per_file`, so its later matches
are missing from this answer while every other file answers in full. `files` names
the cut files in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them. Narrow
`pattern` or `paths`, or raise the `[search]` key `pattern_matches_per_file`.

prepared.description:
Rows of stored file text the trigram index holds: one per file, or one per
chunk of a file split under `[search.text]`.

total.description: Rows of stored file text the store holds.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The trigram index `pattern` selects its files through lacks rows of stored file
text, and verifying those rows beside the selected ones would pass the `[search]`
key `pattern_candidate_rows` or `pattern_verified_size`, so the answer covers the
rows the index holds and a match in the other rows is missing from it. The server
indexes those rows in the background after each write; `prepared` and `total` state
how far it has got. Resend the request once the index has caught up.

unit.description:
The file the warning names. Absent on the one warning that counts the files
past `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX`.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
A file answers nothing from its bytes. Either the index left the claimed file out -
its bytes are not valid UTF-8, or it crosses a per-file bound - so it answers no
search or lookup, and addressing it directly still refuses `content_unavailable`;
or a comparison against the working tree read the changed file in no working form -
its attributes name a `filter` driver or a UTF-16 `working-tree-encoding` - so it
answers changed with no declarations. Every other file in the workspace stays
available. At most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of this warning name a file, in
project-path order; when more files are named, one more carries no `unit` and
counts the rest. `rift server logs` names each file the index left out, and `paths`
narrows a comparison onto the others.

skipped.description: The files past `max_chunk` the request's `paths` reach.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
Text files past `[search.text] max_chunk` are left out of the text index under the
key `large_files = "skip"`, so no hit answers from their text; `skipped` counts the
ones the request's `paths` reach. A declaration such a file holds still answers.
Setting `large_files` to `split` indexes them in chunks.

files.description: The files held as text alone.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
Files past `[providers.syntax] max_file` are held as text the syntax provider does
not parse: their text answers `search`, and none of their declarations were
extracted, so no symbol hit and no `get_symbol` answer comes from them. `files`
names them in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them. Raising
`max_file` parses them.

files.description: The selected lockfiles search leaves out.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
A lockfile the request's `paths.include` selects is left out of search, so no hit
answers from it; `rift://map` still carries the versions it pins. Naming the file
in `paths.force_include` searches it for one request, and removing its name from
the `[search.text]` key `excluded_lockfiles` indexes it. One warning names every
such file, in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them.

symbol.description: The symbol whose presentation facts disagree.

providers.description:
Providers whose Contribution carries a differing value for at least one
presentation field, sorted and deduplicated.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
Contributions selected for one symbol's presentation disagree on at least one
field. The answer carries what normalization selected.

visited.description: Symbols the walk visited before it stopped, equal to the bound it hit.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
A traversal walk stopped at its node bound before exhausting the reachable graph,
so hits reachable beyond the bound are missing from this answer. Narrow the walk -
a tighter `facets` list, a smaller `depth`, or a less-connected seed - to fit it
under the bound.

facets.description:
The requested facets no lane populates, in the request's own order,
deduplicated. Absent when every requested facet has a lane.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
No lane populates part of the relationship coverage the traversal asked for, so the
walk had nothing to follow there whatever the graph holds. The warning states that a
lane is absent; it never states that the seed has no such neighbor. An empty answer
carrying it means the walk could not run; an empty answer without it means the walk
ran and the seed has no neighbor under the request.

language.description: The seed declaration's language, whose engine's answer was dropped.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
A language engine serves the seed's language, and this read carries none of its
edges: the engine answered about bytes the served revision does not carry, answered
more than the walk's node bound holds, or was still analyzing when
`[server] readiness_timeout` was spent. The indexed relationships stand; whatever
the engine resolves on top of them is missing. The warning states that an engine's
analysis is absent from this answer; it never states that the seed has no such
neighbor. An engine still analyzing keeps loading, and a later read, served from a
revision the engine has caught up with or sent once it reads ready, carries the
engine's edges again.

callees.description: Edges the walk dropped over every depth, one per call the engine named.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
An outgoing walk dropped its edges to callees it named no declaration for. The
language engine's call hierarchy named each in a file outside the project and every
installed package the workspace's dependencies name, or in a package or standard
library file where the global index answered no declaration at the callee's
position. Every package callee drops when the global API is off or did not answer,
and the answer then carries the global warning naming why. Every other edge stands.
The warning states that edges are missing from this answer; it never states that
the seed calls nothing more.

processes.description:
The engines the walk took unconfirmed, by accepted process key, sorted. Inline
processes use the exact language identity segment.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The walk took a language engine's answer without progress evidence that the engine
had settled: it announced no work since it started or was last told of a changed
file, and stayed quiet past its `settle_delay`. The answer stands. An engine that
recomputes without announcing work may have answered before it read that change, and
a later read meets it settled.

analyzed.description: Commits the history store holds of the ones its latest fill selects.

total.description: Commits the history store's latest fill selects.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The history store the server fills in the background has not analyzed every commit
`[providers.history]` selects, so a commit search answers from the `analyzed` ones
alone and a commit the store has not reached answers nothing. The fill runs newest
first and continues without a request; a later search answers the rest.

paths_max.description: Changed paths the comparison stopped at, equal to the bound it reached.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The comparison reached `paths_max` changed paths and stopped there, so declarations
in the changed paths past it are missing from this answer. Narrow the comparison
with `paths`, or name two sides that differ in fewer files.

Global access is disabled under `[global] enabled = false`, so the answer carries no
package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the global API failure.

oneOf.description: The global API could not answer, so the answer carries no package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the incompatible publication.

oneOf.description:
The global API advertised a publication the client cannot read, so the answer
carries no package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the invalid response.

oneOf.description:
The global API returned an invalid or truncated response, so the answer carries no
package facts.

warning_code.description:
Stable condition code returned by the global package service, or
`capability_unavailable` for a feature its capabilities do not advertise.

detail.description:
Optional bounded explanation returned by the global package service, or the
feature its capabilities do not advertise.

oneOf.description:
The global package page carried a bounded condition while its items remained valid.
`warning_code` identifies the condition and `detail` carries its bounded explanation.
`capability_unavailable` also names a feature the global API's capabilities do not
advertise, such as `patterns` for a `pattern` search, and the answer then carries the
project hits alone.

package.description: The exact package absent from the global publication.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release of an exact package the dependency
context names, so nothing answers for it. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package
and dependency-context warnings ride one answer.

entry.description: The declared requirement absent from the global publication.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release a declared requirement admits, so nothing
answers for it. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context
warnings ride one answer.

entry.description: The dependency context entry, as the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state it.

package.description: The collected release that answers for `entry`.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release at the exact version the dependency context
names, or none inside the range a declared requirement states, so the collected
release nearest it answers in its place: the package facts for `entry` come from
`package`. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context warnings
ride one answer.

entry.description:
The dependency context entry, as the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state
it; its `availability` names the kind.

reason.description: Why no global package index answers for the entry, for a reader.

oneOf.description:
The dependency context names a package no public registry serves: a path outside
the workspace, a git repository, a private registry, or a URL. No global package
index answers for it, and `reason` names the capability Rift does not have yet. At
most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context warnings ride one
answer.

resolver.description:
What degraded: a resolver by its manager name, `cargo`, `uv`, `npm`, or `bun`, a
standard library entry, `stdlib/rust`, `stdlib/node`, or `stdlib/python`, or the
package manager whose held or requested entries left past the entry bound, such
as `pypi`.

reason.description: What the resolver could not do - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
One resolver or standard library probe read less than the workspace states, or the
context passed the bound on the entries one read carries, the smaller of the
server's own and the one the global API advertises, and its entries sorted last left:
every held entry before any the request's `packages` names. The dependency context
may then miss packages or name a standard library by its static reading. Rides only an answer whose `scope`
reaches packages; at most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context
warnings ride one answer, this one first, in resolver order.

ReadWarning.description:
One warning attached to a read result. The answer stands; the warning carries evidence
of a condition the caller weighs before relying on it.

RelationshipFacet.description:
One portable category an edge falls into. The local kinds `import` and `use` can share
the `imports` facet, which lets one query cross languages.

RevisionId.description:
Identity of one revision in the workspace's version-control history, spelled the way the
version-control system spells it: a branch, tag, or commit id, optionally followed by
ancestry suffixes, such as `HEAD~2` for the second first-parent ancestor or `main^2` for
the second parent. Rift carries it opaquely and never orders two revisions by comparing
their identifiers.

Revision.description: One point on the history axis. `rift://revision/git/<commit>` names a complete git commit id, and `rift://revision/git/<reference>` a branch, tag, or `HEAD` with optional `~N` suffixes that the server resolves to a commit. `rift://revision/<manager>/<registry>/<name>@<version>` names a package release, `rift://revision/stdlib/<runtime>@<version>` a runtime release, and `rift://revision/tree/<digest>` one served working tree. An answer names a commit, a release, or a tree, never a reference.

view.description:
The captured serving context returned by an earlier search. The server retains
query, filters, ranking policy, selected projects and releases under this view.
An expired or mismatched view is unavailable; the server never substitutes latest.

target.description:
Which entity kinds may be returned - a kind selector, never the text to search for;
that is `query`. Omitted, `all`: declarations, tree entries, and documentation
blocks. `commit` matches `query` against the messages of the commits the history
store holds - under `[providers.history] strategy = "selective"`, the selected
releases alone - and answers the commits carrying every term before the ones
carrying some, each group newest first, whatever `order` names. While the store
fills, a commit it has not analyzed yet answers nothing. The server refuses `commit`
beside `pattern`, `traversal`, `change`, `rev`, `packages`, and `paths`, and with a
`scope` past `local`, since each of them selects declarations, text, or another
tree, and the global index holds no project history.

order.description: Which total order the page comes back in. Omitted, relevance.

query.description:
Text to match against declaration names, qualified names, signatures, attached
documentation, and file contents. A declaration whose body alone holds the terms
answers through its file's contents, tagged `content`, when that file ranks among
the first 20 files. Matching is case-insensitive and identifier-aware: the query and
the indexed names split on case, acronym, and separator boundaries, so `loadConfig`
finds `load_config`. Under `relevance`, the server ranks an identifier matching the
original declaration name or qualified name before case-insensitive fallback.
Double quotes keep a phrase together, and an identifier written
inside a question reaches its declaration without being quoted. A query naming
several terms ranks the remaining declarations carrying all of them before the ones
carrying some. Scoring is server-defined and comparable within one answer. With
`target: "commit"`, the text matches commit messages instead.

pattern.description:
A regex matched against the text of every indexed file, in the syntax of the Rust
`regex` crate that ripgrep reads. Matching runs line by line: `^` and `$` match at
line boundaries, a `\r` before a line feed belongs to its line, and no class matches
a line feed, so only a literal `\n` crosses a line; `(?i)` makes the match
case-insensitive. Every match becomes one file hit whose `range` is the match's
bytes, and every declaration holding a match one symbol hit at its first match;
each hit is tagged `content` and carries no score, and `relevance` orders the hits
by path, then offset. With a `scope` past `local`, the global index matches the
pattern over the dependency packages' source too, and those hits carry `unit` in
place of `path`. The server refuses `pattern` beside `query`, `traversal`,
`change`, and `rev`, and with `target: "documentation"`, and it refuses a pattern
whose compiled size, candidate rows, or verified bytes pass the `[search]` bounds,
naming the bound.

scope.description:
Which sources `query` and `pattern` search: the project tree, the dependency
packages, or both. Omitted, `local`. A package contributes symbol hits alone to
`query`, and file and symbol hits to `pattern`. The server refuses a scope beyond
`local` together with `rev`, since package facts are served for the current tree
alone, and `global` together with `traversal`, since a walk runs over the project
alone.

packages.description:
Packages `query` and `pattern` search beside the ones the workspace's manifests and
lockfiles name, at most 64. An entry naming a package the workspace depends on replaces that
package's versions for this search, and an entry naming another package adds it.
The server refuses `packages` beside the `local` scope, since a project search
consults no package, and beside `rev`, since package facts are served for the
current tree alone.

paths.description:
Files eligible for the search, selected by project-relative globs. Omitted selects
every visible file.

include.description:
Extra payload to attach to every hit. Every entry costs response bytes per hit, so
the caller requests only what it will read.

limit.description:
Most hits to return in one page, at most 10,000; the server refuses a larger
`limit` naming the field. The server's result bound caps the set itself, and an
answer whose set reached it warns `results_truncated`.

page_index.description:
Zero-based page of the result set to serve, sized by `limit`. A `page_index` past
the last page returns an empty page whose `pagination` carries the requested
`page_index` and the true `total_pages`.

revision.description:
The revision to search: a git revision searches that commit, a tree revision the
served working tree. Omitted searches the served working tree. The server refuses a
git revision when the workspace has no version-control repository, a tree revision
once the index serves another tree, and a release revision, since `packages` names
the releases a search reads.

traversal.description:
A bounded relationship walk from `seed`, standing alone or beside `query`. A symbol
the walk reaches becomes a hit tagged `relationship`; one also matched lexically
keeps its own score and payload and gains the walk's path. `target: "file"` never
carries a walked hit, since a traversal only reaches symbols. With no `query`,
`relevance` orders hits by ascending `distance`, then identity. A configured
language engine resolves the references the walk follows, and an engine session
serves the current tree, so the server refuses `traversal` beside `rev` and beside
`change`.

change.description:
A committed revision compared against another revision or the working tree,
standing alone. Every declaration the two sides hold differently becomes a hit
tagged `change`, carrying a `change` block that names what differs and where the
declaration lives on each side. `target: "file"` never carries a change hit, since
the comparison reaches declarations alone, and `relevance` orders the hits by path,
then name. `paths` narrows which changed paths are compared. The server refuses
`change` beside `rev`, since `change` names its own revisions; beside `query`, since
the two select different result sets; beside `traversal`, which no comparison
serves; and beside a `scope` past `local`.

SearchParams.description:
Criteria for one search. The caller supplies a lexical `query`, a relationship
`traversal`, or both, a regex `pattern`, or a `change` comparing a committed revision
against another revision or the working tree; `paths` narrows the files eligible for any
of them.

allOf.description: a search selects its result set with query, pattern, traversal, or change
a traversal never rides beside change

SearchParamsTarget.description: Which entity kinds may be returned.

ResultOrder.description:
The total order a paginated answer comes back in. Every order ends in the result's own

manager.description: Package manager or ecosystem name, as `cargo`, `npm`, or `pypi`.

registry.description: Accepted defining registry endpoint. Absent when the registry is unresolved.

version.description:
The exact version to read. Absent, the entry asks for the requirement `>=0`, which
the global index answers from its newest collected release.

RequestedPackage.description: One package a `get_symbol` or `search` request names beside the dependency context.

include.description: Globs a path has to match to be searched at all. Empty includes every visible file.

exclude.description: Globs that drop a path `include` already matched.

force_include.description:
Globs reaching files the workspace's `[source]` policy or `.gitignore` excluded from
the index. Matches are bounded per request - the bound counts the files the request
reaches outside the index, so a glob whose matches the index already holds adds none -
and the server refuses the search when the bound is crossed rather than truncating it
silently.

PathSelector.description:
Which files a query runs over, as three lists of globs matched against the project-relative
path. The same glob engine backs the workspace's `[source]` policy. `include: ["src/**"]`
selects the source tree; `exclude: ["src/generated/**"]` then removes generated output.

PathPattern.description:
Project-relative glob using *, ?, **, and character classes. Forward-slash separated on
every platform, whatever separator the host OS uses natively.

SearchInclude.description:
Extra payload to attach to every hit. Every entry costs response bytes per hit, so the
caller requests only what it will read.

The revision compared from - a branch, tag, or commit id as the workspace's version

head.description:

SearchChange.description:
Two sides to compare. The answer is the declarations the two sides hold differently:

compared to.

The working tree as the current index serves it: staged and unstaged edits, files

The side a comparison compares to: a committed revision, or the working tree with its

oneOf.description: The working tree, uncommitted edits included.

ChangeTree.description:
A comparison side that names a tree rather than a revision, spelled

The captured serving context for this result, including an empty page. Each hit
carries the original view of its selected project or released owner.
Absent when the caller selected latest facts without retained serving context.

Absent when the answer merged several project trees, read packages alone, or

warnings.description: Warnings attached to this result. Absent when there is nothing to warn about.

A comparison that reaches the bound answers from the paths that fit and warns change_truncated.

SearchUnavailable.description: The captured selection cannot serve this search or pattern request.

symbol.description:
The symbol whose nodes the read lists: each declaration's item node, then the
descendants that belong to that declaration and not to a declaration nested in it,
outermost first per declaration. A package or runtime symbol's nodes come from the
global API. The caller MUST omit `path` and `position` beside it.

path.description: Project-relative file to inspect. The caller MUST send it together with `position`.

position.description:
UTF-8 byte offset inside the declaration whose nodes the read lists - one position,
not a range; the nodes themselves carry the spans. The read lists the nodes of the
innermost declaration holding the node at the position, or of the file's unit when no
declaration holds it. A position inside a multi-byte character is valid; a position at
or past the file's byte length refuses.

view.description:
Captured view selected by discovery. The server reads nodes from that view and
refuses an expired or foreign view. The caller MUST omit `revision` beside `view`.

revision.description:
The revision to read: a git revision reads that commit, a tree revision the served
working tree, and a release revision selects the release of a package or runtime
`symbol`'s owner. Omitted reads the served working tree, or for a package the version
the workspace's dependencies pin, else the newest collected release. The server refuses
a git revision when the workspace has no version-control repository, and a tree
revision once the index serves another tree.

NodesParams.description:
Lists syntax nodes with their source: every node of one `symbol`, or the nodes of the
innermost declaration holding one `position` in one file, or of that file's unit when no
declaration holds it. Each node carries its kind, range, source text, and place, including
expressions smaller than a declaration.

allOf.description: nodes selects a symbol, or a path with a position

symbol.description:
The symbol whose declarations hold the listed nodes: the requested one for a `symbol`
read, the innermost declaration's symbol for a `position` read. Absent when the nodes
belong to a unit outside every declaration.

nodes.description:
Nodes the read selected, in pre-order: per declaration, in the order a symbol read
lists them, or the unit's nodes from its file node on.

node_cursor.description:
Continuation for the rest of an answer whose nodes crossed its node count or source
byte bound. Absent when the answer holds the last node.

revision.description: The revision this answer was read at: a commit, a release, or a working tree.

view.description:
Captured view used for this read, with its original expiry. Absent when the
request did not select a captured view.

warnings.description: Warnings attached to this result. Absent when there is nothing to warn about.

NodesResult.description:
The nodes a read selected, each with its source text and its place inside its symbol or
unit.

declaration.description:
Ordinal of the declaration holding this node among the declarations of the symbol the
read names, from 0 in the order a symbol read lists them. Absent for a node outside
every declaration: the file node, an import, a top-level statement.

index.description:
Pre-order position of this node inside its declaration's item subtree, or inside its
unit when `declaration` is absent. The item node and the unit's file node are 0.

unit.description:
The source unit the node is written in: a project file, as
`rift://source/project/src/lib.rs`, or a package or runtime source unit for a node of
a package or runtime symbol. It names no revision; the answer's `revision` does.

language.description:
The grammar that produced this node. It belongs to the identity because two
providers can produce different trees over the same file bytes.

kind.description:
What the node is in the provider's vocabulary, such as `fn_item`, `mapping.key`, or
`selector.class`.

facets.description:
Portable structural classification, so a query can ask for bodies or imports without
knowing the grammar that produced them. Absent when empty.

range.description: The bytes it spans, as offsets into the file.

source.description: The node's exact source text: the bytes `range` spans at the read's revision.

regions.description: The node's named parts, including its function body and documentation. Absent when empty.

parent.description:
`index` of the node this one is nested inside, in the same declaration or unit. Absent
for node 0.

extensions.description:
Syntax facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted
them. Absent when empty.

Node.description:
One node of a source unit's syntax tree, with its source text, addressed by its place inside
a symbol. A node inside a declaration's item subtree is node `index` of declaration
`declaration` of the symbol the read names; a node outside every declaration is node `index`
of its `unit`. Indexes count in pre-order from 0 at the declaration's item node, or from 0 at
the unit's file node, and skip the subtrees of nested declarations, whose nodes belong to the
nested symbol. The address names a place at the read's revision: an edit renumbers the nodes
after it.

Portable structural facets, so a filter can ask for bodies or imports without knowing the
grammar that produced them.
